title: The homotopy category of a braided category is braided (Koszul braiding)
statement:
Let $C$ be a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category] with a zero object and a monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category], additive in each tensor variable, and a braiding $\beta$ (natural isomorphisms satisfying both hexagon identities). Let $I$ be an additive commutative monoid with decidable equality. A complex shape $c$ is a relation on $I$ with at most one successor and at most one predecessor at each index. Assume its relation is preserved by adding an index, and fix a homomorphism $\varepsilon:I\to\{1,-1\}$ with $\varepsilon(p')=-\varepsilon(p)$ whenever $c(p,p')$. A $c$-complex has objects $X^p$ and maps $d_X^{p,p'}$ zero off $c(p,p')$, with consecutive differentials composing to zero. Its maps commute with differentials. A homotopy from $f$ to $f'$ is a family $h^{i,j}:X^i\to X'^j$ zero unless $c(j,i)$ and satisfying $f-f'=d_{X'}h+hd_X$; the sums here have at most two terms at each index.

Assume the usual total tensor monoidal structure on $\operatorname{Ch}_c(C)$ is defined: $(X\otimes Y)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}X^p\otimes Y^q$, with summand differential $d_X\otimes1+\varepsilon(p)1\otimes d_Y$, unit $\mathbf1[0]$, unsigned associator induced by that of $C$ and reindexing triple coproducts, and unitors induced by those of $C$. The iterated tensor coproducts used here have their usual universal properties (in particular triple-summand inclusions detect equality). This is the total/graded tensor availability hypothesis, not a finite-coproduct assertion for unbounded integer complexes.

Fix signs $\sigma:I\times I\to\{1,-1\}$ satisfying
$$\sigma(p',q)=\varepsilon(q)\sigma(p,q)\quad(c(p,p')),\qquad \sigma(p,q')=\varepsilon(p)\sigma(p,q)\quad(c(q,q')),$$
and the two coherence identities
$$\sigma(p,q+r)=\sigma(p,q)\sigma(p,r),\qquad\sigma(p+q,r)=\sigma(p,r)\sigma(q,r).$$
Then the summand formula $\sigma(p,q)\beta_{X^p,Y^q}$ defines a natural chain isomorphism $B_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\otimes X$. It induces a braiding on $K_c(C)$, the category with the same complexes as objects and chain maps modulo homotopy as morphisms, for its total tensor monoidal structure: both hexagon identities hold, and the quotient functor sends $B_{X,Y}$ to this braiding. For $I=\mathbf Z$, $c(p,p')\iff p'=p+1$, $\varepsilon(p)=(-1)^p$ and $\sigma(p,q)=(-1)^{pq}$, this is exactly the Koszul braiding. Symmetry of $C$ is not required.

proof.text: First define $[f]\otimes[g]=[f\otimes g]$ on the homotopy quotient. Apply [lem-pur-shape-total-tensor-homotopies] separately in the two variables: replacing $f$ by $f'$ changes the tensor by a homotopy, and then replacing $g$ by $g'$ does so again. Add the two homotopies. Composition respects homotopy because composing $f-f'=dh+hd$ with a chain map $u$ gives the homotopy $uh$ or $hu$, respectively. Identity and composition for the tensor therefore follow from those on complexes. Use the classes of the already given complex associators and unitors as constraints; their inverse, naturality, pentagon and triangle equations are preserved by $Q(fg)=Q(f)Q(g)$. All objects of the quotient are complexes and all its morphisms are represented by chain maps, so these equations hold on every object and morphism. This gives the total tensor monoidal structure on $K_c(C)$ with $Q$ preserving tensor and constraints. Only preadditivity and the assumed total tensor availability are used; no abelian or K-flat hypotheses enter.

proof.text: For each $p+q=n$, map the source summand to the target summand indexed by $(q,p)$ by $\sigma(p,q)\beta_{X^p,Y^q}$. The coproduct universal property assembles these into $B^n$. Its degreewise inverse uses $\sigma(p,q)\beta_{X^p,Y^q}^{-1}$ on that target summand. Indeed both composites are identity since $\sigma(p,q)^2=1$; the inverse uses the inverse braiding, not a symmetry assumption. For a differential arrow $p\to p'$, the coefficients of the two composites in the chain-map square are $\sigma(p',q)$ and $\varepsilon(q)\sigma(p,q)$. For $q\to q'$, they are $\varepsilon(p)\sigma(p,q')$ and $\sigma(p,q)$. The assumed differential sign equations make each pair equal, while naturality of the underlying braiding identifies the unsigned maps. Off the shape relation both maps are zero. Hence $B$ is a chain map, and its degreewise inverse commutes with differentials by multiplying this square by the inverses. The construction is therefore a chain isomorphism.

source.place: Section section-symmetric-monoidal immediately before Tag 0FNI (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes): explicit chain-map sign calculation, generalized from (-1)^(pq) to sigma.

proof.text: For chain maps $f:X\to X'$ and $g:Y\to Y'$, apply [lem-sfb-braiding-naturality] in $C$ to $f^p$ and $g^q$. Multiply the equality by $\sigma(p,q)$ and then include its target into the $(q,p)$ coproduct summand. Coproduct uniqueness yields $B_{X',Y'}\circ(f\otimes g)=(g\otimes f)\circ B_{X,Y}$. This proves naturality in both variables, with inverse naturality following by composing with $B^{-1}$.

source.place: Section section-symmetric-monoidal and Tag 0FNI; componentwise naturality for the braided generalization.

proof.text: For the hexagon involving $B_{X,Y\otimes Z}$, test on $X^p\otimes(Y^q\otimes Z^r)$, inserting the specified unsigned associators to compare the two parenthesizations. The path that swaps $X$ with $Y\otimes Z$ has coefficient $\sigma(p,q+r)$; the path that first swaps it with $Y$ and then with $Z$ has coefficient $\sigma(p,q)\sigma(p,r)$. These are equal by the first coherence hypothesis. After removing this common scalar, the equality is the formula for $\beta_{A,B\otimes D}$ in [lem-sfb-braiding-hexagon], with $A=X^p$, $B=Y^q$, $D=Z^r$. Tensor additivity ensures that the signs multiply under the two successive tensor maps. Triple-summand inclusions detect equality by hypothesis, so this proves the hexagon as an equality of chain maps.

source.place: Tag 0FNI, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, omitted diagram verification: first hexagon supplied explicitly by the sigma(p,q+r) calculation.

proof.text: For the other hexagon, test on $(X^p\otimes Y^q)\otimes Z^r$. Swapping $X\otimes Y$ with $Z$ contributes $\sigma(p+q,r)$; swapping $Y$ with $Z$ and then $X$ with $Z$ contributes $\sigma(q,r)\sigma(p,r)$. The second coherence hypothesis and commutativity of the sign group identify these coefficients. The unsigned equality is precisely the formula for $\beta_{A\otimes B,D}$ in [lem-sfb-braiding-hexagon], with $A=X^p$, $B=Y^q$, $D=Z^r$. Again the given associators carry no sign, and triple-summand uniqueness proves equality on the total complexes. No equality $\beta_{B,A}\beta_{A,B}=1$ is used.

proof.text: Set $\overline B_{X,Y}=Q(B_{X,Y})$, with inverse $Q(B_{X,Y}^{-1})$. The inverse equations survive under $Q$. By step 1, a morphism in either variable is represented by a chain map and the quotient tensor is its tensor class; applying $Q$ to the naturality equation in step 3 proves naturality for every quotient morphism. Applying $Q$ to the two equalities in steps 4 and 5 gives exactly the two quotient hexagons, since step 1 defined the quotient associators and tensor on maps as their images. Thus $\overline B$ is a braiding on the specified monoidal category $K_c(C)$.

proof.text: For integer cochain complexes, $\varepsilon(p+1)=-\varepsilon(p)$ and the differential sign equations are $(p+1)q=pq+q$ and $p(q+1)=pq+p$ modulo $2$. The two coherence equations follow from $p(q+r)=pq+pr$ and $(p+q)r=pr+qr$. Therefore the canonical signs $(-1)^{pq}$ satisfy all the hypotheses, for negative integers as well as positive ones, and the summand formula in step 2 is exactly the claimed Koszul formula.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-O3-7f175a656 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new leaf, the four cited statements, the upstream Braided.lean (lines 174-244), Mathlib ComplexShapeSigns (TensorSigns 117-126, the TotalComplexShape c c c instance 158-166, TotalComplexShapeSymmetry 290-302) and BifunctorHomotopy (hypotheses 28-37, declarations at lines 178 and 190), plus Stacks 0FNI, 0GWP and lemma-derived-tor-homotopy. The STATEMENT-DISPUTED correction is right. The upstream general instance assumes only σ_ε₁ and σ_ε₂. For the (c,c,c) shape these are exactly the item's two differential equations, and they still hold when σ is replaced by −σ. With −σ the hexagon on ℚ[0] would need −1 = 1, and degree-0 complexes have no homotopies, so the general upstream statement is false and the added multiplicativity hypotheses are needed. The integer Koszul case is kept exactly (step 7), and that is the only case the citer thm-asd-smooth-tensor needs. Dropping the stmt_dep def-kun-derived-tensor is correct because it was unused. I recomputed the step-2 chain-map coefficients: σ(p',q) against ε(q)σ(p,q), and ε(p)σ(p,q') against σ(p,q). The inverse uses β⁻¹, not β_{Y,X}. The hexagon scalars are σ(p,q+r) against σ(p,q)σ(p,r), and σ(p+q,r) against σ(q,r)σ(p,r). I type-checked both formulas of lem-sfb-braiding-hexagon against Mathlib's hexagon_forward and hexagon_reverse. The (c,c,c) associator is unsigned, and triple-summand detection is an explicit hypothesis. The new leaf is an exact one-declaration-per-clause specialisation (F = curriedTensor) and is strictly smaller than the item. It is not a duplicate of lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy, which covers only integer cochains in an abelian category with all colimits. Its blueprint.from.node is null, which matches what blueprint_refs.ancestor_for_item returns for this maintainer-created item. No SGA source is used and no changes were made. Stage 2 must deal with the false general Lean instance.
